answer: Independent multi-verifier approval resists Sybil attacks: a new identity gains full weight only after three unrelated verifiers — a hardware attestation service, a payment processor, and a work-history registry — each independently confirm it, like light through a prism splitting into beams that must reconverge. A fake nebula of aliases may pass one check, but passing all three for thousands of identities requires forging credentials across separate systems, so cost multiplies with each verifier, and one failed check at the zenith of approval revokes the identity before it can transact.
